title: Universal spin-squeezing dynamics in spinor condensates
authors: Nikolaos Giovanoudis, Navid Kazemiseresht, Fabio Mezzacapo, Emilia Witkowska, Tommaso Roscilde
abstract: The production of large-scale entangled states is one of the main goals of next-generation quantum technologies, with an immediate potential for applications in the context of entanglement-assisted quantum sensing. A very promising platform to achieve this goal is offered by ultracold spinor gases, made of atoms with a large internal spin sensitive to magnetic fields. Here we show that the native spin-changing collisions in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate, combined with an arbitrary quadratic Zeeman shift, can generate scalable spin squeezing in the collective spin of the ensemble, following the universal paradigm of the celebrated one-axis-twisting model. Squeezing dynamics is driven by the quadratic Zeeman shift when this shift is small; and by the spin-changing collisions for large shifts, in the form of stroboscopic squeezing. Turning off the Zeeman shift freezes out the collective-spin dynamics, so that the ensuing collective spin dynamics can be uniquely governed by an external field to be sensed. Our theoretical results pave the way for the use of spinor Bose gases with a large spin in fundamental studies of entanglement, as well as in advanced metrological applications.
summary: This paper demonstrates how spinor Bose-Einstein condensates can generate scalable spin squeezing using native spin interactions combined with a quadratic Zeeman shift. The dynamics are shown to follow universal paradigms, exhibiting different behaviors depending on the relative strength of the applied magnetic field parameter ($q$). This control mechanism is highly valuable for developing advanced quantum sensors.
main_problem: The primary goal is generating large-scale entangled states for quantum sensing using ultracold spinor Bose-Einstein condensates.
main_result: Spin squeezing can be generated universally in these condensates, exhibiting distinct dynamics depending on the relative strength of spin-dependent interactions versus the quadratic Zeeman shift (OAT vs. stroboscopic regimes).
method: The authors employ theoretical analysis using perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff transformation) and exact numerical diagonalization to model the system's evolution.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate of atoms with large internal spin ($S>1/2$). The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian incorporating both spin-dependent contact interactions and a quadratic Zeeman shift term.
key_observables: Spin squeezing parameter ($\xi_R^2$), which quantifies entanglement, and the optimal time for achieving minimum $\xi_R^2$.
important_parameters: The ratio of the quadratic Zeeman shift ($q$) to interaction strengths, leading to distinct regimes: $|q| \ll 1$ (OAT-like) and $|q| \gg 1$ (stroboscopic).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on projecting dynamics onto a restricted subspace (e.g., the Dicke subspace) using perturbation theory, which is valid under specific parameter limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spin squeezing dynamics across different $q$ regimes, showing OAT-like evolution for small $|q|$ and stroboscopic behavior for large $|q|$. Scaling laws are also presented.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by deriving effective Hamiltonians for different limits of the quadratic Zeeman shift ($|q| \ll 1$ vs. $|q| \gg 1$), comparing theoretical predictions with exact numerical simulations to map out universal squeezing dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, controllable mechanism for generating high levels of entanglement in an ultracold atomic system, offering significant potential for quantum metrology beyond standard qubit platforms.

(a)-(b) Scaling of the best squeezing (ξ2 R)min and the best squeezing time tmin with system size N obtained from exact diagonalization, demonstrating the OAT scaling (ξ2 R)min ∼N −2/3 and tmin ∼N 1/3 across the explored values of N. FIG. 3: Freezing of squeezed states. If q is turned off abruptly, the remaining Hamiltonian is SU(2) symmetric, so that the ensuing dynamics does not evolve the collective-spin properties, including squeezing.
